Elaborating this fact, it is the case of the applicant that the complainant has lodged the case against two unknown persons.
The accused (applicant) was arrested on 08.05.2023 and presently, he is in judicial custody.

Investigation, in the present case, is stated to be complete and no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in the judicial custody.

sentences.text: Apart from this, number of undertakings have also been given on behalf of the applicant, for which, the applicant is ready to abide by, in case, ordered to be released on bail, during the pendency of the trial.

5. The applicant has earlier tried his luck before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), Shimla, H.P., by filing a bail application, however, the said application was dismissed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, vide order dated 07.08.2023.

sentences.text: 6. Apart from this, the applicant has also asserted the fact that during the pendency of the proceedings before the learned trial Court, the informer has stated that he has no objection if the bail is granted to the applicant.

In this regard, the applicant has relied upon the affidavit/statement of the complainant Ext. P-1 and Ext. P-2.
7.
On the basis of above facts, Sh. Jagmohan Singh Chandel, learned counsel appearing for the applicant has prayed that during the pendency of the trial, the applicant may kindly be released on bail.

8. When put to notice, the police has filed the status report, disclosing therein, that on 08.05.2023,
the mother of the child victim has telephonically informed the police that she is residing with her children.
Her husband is serving at Solan.

She had received the telephonic call from the child victim,
disclosing therein, that two unknown persons trespassed in their house and they had damaged electricity bulb, as such, a prayer has been made to send the police.

8.1. On the basis of said information, SI/SHO along- with other police officials reached at the spot, where, the complainant,
who is father of the child victim, submitted a complaint to the police, disclosing therein, that he was married in the year 2005 and blessed with five children, out of which, three are daughters and two are sons.
The wife of the complainant is working as Safai Karamchari in the Hospital at place 'X'.
At his native place, his mother along- with five children of this witness is residing.

Her mother, on 07.05.2023, had gone to the house of his relative and complainant had gone to another village to attend the 'Jagran'.
8.2.
At about 12.00 in the night, the mother of the complainant informed him that two unknown persons trespassed into their home and damaged the electricity bulb.

She has requested him to come back and after reaching at his native place, he inquired from his children about the incident,
upon which, they had disclosed that some unknown person had done wrong act with the child victim.

Thereafter, he has also inquired this fact from the child victim, who, on inquiry disclosed that one, out of two unknown persons, was Akshay Kumar, resident of Aahnog (applicant) and the other person is not known to her.
The age of the child victim has been mentioned as 14 years.
8.3. On the basis of above facts, he has prayed that action be taken against the accused persons.

8.4. 
On the basis of above facts, the police registered FIR under Sections 458, 376-D, 34 IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and the criminal machinery swung into motion.

8.5. The child victim was firstly referred to CHC, Kupvi for her medico legal examination, from where, she was referred to CH,
Nerwa.
On 08.05.2023, both the accused persons were arrested and were medico legally examined.

8.6. After completion of the investigation the police has submitted the report under Section 173(2)

thereafter, when the report from DNA Division, SFSL Junga was received, then, the supplementary challan has been filed.

8.7. Lastly, it has been apprehended that in case, the applicant is released on bail, he may coerce the witnesses to depose in his favour, as such, a prayer has been made to dismiss the application.
9.
The investigation, in the present case, is complete as it is the stand of the police that report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C has been filed against the applicant.
Even, the DNA report has also been submitted to the trial Court, by way of supplementary challan.
In such situation, it can be concluded that custodial interrogation of the applicant is neither required nor sought for by the police, in this case.

10. Considering the fact that in the initial information to the police, the allegations against two unknown persons were levelled, the applicant is entitled for the relief, as claimed by him in the present case.
Even otherwise, the role allegedly played by the applicant, in the commission of the offences, will be proved during the course of trial.
11. No other criminal history of the applicant has been pleaded or argued by the learned Additional Advocate General, as such, presumption of innocence is still available to the applicant.

12. When, the custodial interrogation of the applicant has not been sought, then, keeping him in the judicial custody, that too, for the indefinite period, is nothing, but, punishing him before the trial,
which is prohibited under the law.

13. So far as the apprehensions, which have been expressed by the police, in the status report, are concerned, for those apprehensions, reasonable conditions can be imposed, in case, the applicant is ordered to be released on bail.

14. So far as the affidavit and statement of the complainant in favour of the applicant is concerned,
the same in no way, helps the case of the applicant, as, the role of the complainant in the cases like the present one, is only to put the criminal machinery into motion and thereafter, he cannot give any concession to anyone including the accused.
15. The crime is always against the State.
In such situation, no benefit could be derived by the applicant from this fact.

16. The applicant has pleaded his age as 19 years, in the application, whereas, in the status report,
his age has been mentioned as 18 years.

Keeping in view the young age of the applicant, in the light of allegations, which have been made against him by the complainant, this Court is of the view that keeping the applicant in the judicial custody, that too, in the company of hardened criminals, would certainly affect his career.
17. Considering all these facts, the applicant is able to make out a case for bail in his favour.
